newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to complete smelter sale by September.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to complete smelter sale by September.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Friday it had signed a preliminary agreement with Belgium's Union Miniere SA for the sale of 56 percent of the MDK copper smelter and hoped to finalise the deal by September.

An agency statement said Union Miniere, which had submitted the winning bid, had offered $80 million and an investment programme worth $220 million, which would make the deal Bulgaria's biggest sell-off so far.
The investment programme is aimed at increasing the plant's smelting capacity and the construction of a new refinery.
The preliminary agreement is pending the approval of the cabinet.

A key issue in the MDK sale has been pollution at the smelter site and the surrounding area and Union Miniere would fund and carry out an environmental study before finalising the deal, the statement said.
The study is expected to take up to eight weeks and the Privatisation Agency and the Belgium firm hope to be able to sign a final agreement by the beginning of September.
The World Bank said last December it was willing to help finance capacity expansion, upgrading and solving MDK's environmental problems once the company is privatised.
Another 30 percent of the plant, whose profit was more than 2.4 billion levs ($1.4 million) last year and some $3 million in 1995, have been offered for mass voucher privatisation.

MDK's turnover was $111.4 million in 1994 and $168 million in 1995. Its annual copper production capacity is up to 50,000 tonnes now, officials said. The plant imports some 30 percent of its raw materials.
Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA bought in April a 60 percent stake in soda ash producer Sodi for $160 million and under the contract will invest $67 million in the next five years.
-- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188 ($ = 1686 Bulgarian Levs)
